brief.l3.text: Create coherent pixel-art status assets for the queue UI. Preserve the existing vector Start control. Status cells are 16 by 16 logical pixels. Working uses four horizontal frames with a 100 ms frame duration. Ready and Retry are static images. Use transparent backgrounds, readable silhouettes and the existing UI's cool blue accent; a fixed palette is not required. Inspect at 1x and 3x nearest display scale on the actual dark panel. The working loop must communicate activity without looking like success. Error/retry must be distinguishable without color alone.

brief.l5.text: Assets belong at the paths already used by the view. Account badges are provided by a server registry and are outside this local asset request. No approved style reference exists yet: propose a representative status sample before expanding the family.

brief.l7.text: Update: the queue now supports a paused state. Its status image must be distinguishable from activity, completion and retry without relying on color alone. Keep the existing style and display requirements. The failure visual moved to the path in the updated view; its purpose is unchanged.

brief.l9.text: Current update: Ready must visibly use a check mark with asymmetrical arms to convey successful completion. The destination now follows the updated view. Keep the existing 16x16 canvas, static behavior, transparent background and review display conditions.

kit.review-route.kind: kit method (mechanical check cannot decide intentional foreground or unwanted matte; split or use visual mode)
kit.review-route.text:
Check the **review route** as well as the wording. A local mechanical check can
establish measured dimensions, frame counts or alpha values. It cannot decide which
shape is intentional foreground, whether a matte is unwanted, whether a silhouette
reads as the requested symbol, or whether an accent serves its role. For a mixed
criterion, either split the measurement and required visual judgment or set its mode
to `visual` (normally domain `visual` too). The runtime requires saved native/enlarged
candidate views for visual-mode or visual/continuity-domain reviews; labelling such a
condition `mechanical`/`local` bypasses that evidence requirement. A planning-only
correction must still specify the route its future acceptance will actually need.

kit.recipe.kind: kit method (required outcome separate from recipe; observations are not rejection rules)
kit.recipe.text:
Keep a required outcome separate from the recipe proposed to achieve it. A qualitative requirement such as matching a reference or conveying a state still needs an acceptance criterion when its palette, geometry, frame count or layout are open. When demoting an unsupported recipe to a sample choice, preserve the underlying required outcome; do not leave only mechanical checks binding. Consumer code establishes its actual data/rendering behavior, not an unmeasured aesthetic quality. Attribute expert quality criteria to expert judgment where that is their basis.

Creative decisions within the assignment need not all go back to the user. For example, choosing a static first sample or a construction method is expert judgment; attributing it to an owner who specified only canvas dimensions is incorrect. Keep the choice explicit and scoped so it can be revised without changing the owner's brief. Observations alone do not become rejection rules.

kit.unlinked.kind: kit spec (authoring view choice expansion; unlinked does not mean irrelevant)
kit.unlinked.text:
The authoring view expands choices through declared semantic links from the
selected outputs/contracts, family destinations, inputs/nominees, decisions and
knowledge. It follows transitive authority links without traversing project
ownership or historical proof. Other project intake choices remain in the compact
`choice_scope.other_intake` index with exact complete-context retrieval arguments.
Project rows explicitly omit `in`; full choice values and their source material
are expanded only when linked. Unlinked does not mean irrelevant: inspect an
indexed choice if applicability is uncertain, and preserve caller instructions.
This selection uses no key/text heuristic and does not change saved I statuses.
